paragraphs.text: Βίβλος γενέσεως Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ υἱοῦ Δαυὶδ υἱοῦ Ἀβραάμ.
paragraphs.translit: Biblos geneseōs Iēsou christou huiou Dauid huiou Abraam.

i18n.en: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.

notes.official: *Biblos geneseōs* — the genealogical incipit deliberately calques Gen 2:4 LXX / Gen 5:1 LXX *biblos geneseōs* (itself rendering Hebrew *sēfer tôlĕdôt* 'book of generations'). The Matthean opening positions the gospel as a *new Genesis*, framing the Jesus-narrative as a creation-typological event in Hebrew Bible-cosmological register. *Iēsou christou* deploys the Greek-Hebrew-Aramaic cognate trio (see glossary `christos-māšîaḥ-anointed-one-cross-corpus-greek-hebrew-aramaic` and `iēsous-yehoshua-yhwh-saves-folk-etymology-cross-corpus`). Davies-Allison ICC 1.149-160; Brown 1993 64-95; Luz Hermeneia 1.81-86.

paragraphs.text: Ἀβραὰμ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰσαάκ, Ἰσαὰκ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ, Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰούδαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ,
paragraphs.translit: Abraam egennēsen ton Isaak, Isaak de egennēsen ton Iakōb, Iakōb de egennēsen ton Ioudan kai tous adelphous autou,

i18n.en: Abraham begot Isaac, and Isaac begot Jacob, and Jacob begot Judah and his brothers,

paragraphs.text: Ἰούδας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Φαρὲς καὶ τὸν Ζαρὰ ἐκ τῆς Θαμάρ, Φαρὲς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἑσρώμ, Ἑσρὼμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀράμ,
paragraphs.translit: Ioudas de egennēsen ton Phares kai ton Zara ek tēs Thamar, Phares de egennēsen ton Hesrōm, Hesrōm de egennēsen ton Aram,

i18n.en: and Judah begot Perez and Zerah by Tamar, and Perez begot Hezron, and Hezron begot Aram,

notes.official: Tamar is the first of four women named in the Matthean genealogy (Tamar / Rahab / Ruth / wife-of-Uriah, plus Mary at v.16). Davies-Allison ICC 1.170-172 list four interpretive readings of the inclusion: (a) the women as sinners (foregrounding divine-grace in irregular-genealogy); (b) the women as foreigners (foregrounding Gentile-inclusion in the Davidic-line); (c) the women as marked by irregular-sexual-unions (preparing the reader for Mary's irregular-conception); (d) divine-providence-through-irregularity (the Davidic-line preserved through divine-initiative). The fourth reading is the modern critical consensus (Brown 1993 73-74; Luz Hermeneia 1.85). The text preserves all four readings without surface-adjudication.

paragraphs.text: Ἀρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀμιναδάβ, Ἀμιναδὰβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ναασσών, Ναασσὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλμών,
paragraphs.translit: Aram de egennēsen ton Aminadab, Aminadab de egennēsen ton Naassōn, Naassōn de egennēsen ton Salmōn,

i18n.en: and Aram begot Amminadab, and Amminadab begot Nahshon, and Nahshon begot Salmon,

paragraphs.text: Σαλμὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Βοὲς ἐκ τῆς Ῥαχάβ, Βοὲς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωβὴδ ἐκ τῆς Ῥούθ, Ἰωβὴδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεσσαί,
paragraphs.translit: Salmōn de egennēsen ton Boes ek tēs Rhachab, Boes de egennēsen ton Iōbēd ek tēs Rhouth, Iōbēd de egennēsen ton Iessai,

i18n.en: and Salmon begot Boaz by Rahab, and Boaz begot Obed by Ruth, and Obed begot Jesse,

paragraphs.text: Ἰεσσαὶ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Δαυὶδ τὸν βασιλέα. Δαυὶδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σολομῶνα ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Οὐρίου,
paragraphs.translit: Iessai de egennēsen ton Dauid ton basilea. Dauid de egennēsen ton Solomōna ek tēs tou Ouriou,

i18n.en: and Jesse begot David the king. And David begot Solomon by the wife of Uriah,

notes.official: *tēs tou Ouriou* — the periphrastic feminine 'her of Uriah' (literally 'the [wife] of Uriah') deliberately AVOIDS naming Bathsheba directly. The naming-by-husband foregrounds the irregular-union (David's appropriation of Uriah's wife per 2 Sam 11) rather than the Bathsheba-figure herself. The Matthean rhetorical strategy preserves the moral-difficulty of the Davidic-line's foundational-irregularity. Davies-Allison ICC 1.174; Brown 1993 75-76; Luz Hermeneia 1.85.

paragraphs.text: Σολομὼν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ῥοβοάμ, Ῥοβοὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιά, Ἀβιὰ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀσάφ,
paragraphs.translit: Solomōn de egennēsen ton Rhoboam, Rhoboam de egennēsen ton Abia, Abia de egennēsen ton Asaph,

i18n.en: and Solomon begot Rehoboam, and Rehoboam begot Abijah, and Abijah begot Asaph,

notes.official: **Textual variant.** Vaticanus (B/03) + Sinaiticus (א/01) + NA28/SBLGNT/THGNT critical text read *Asaph* (the psalmist's name); the Hebrew Bible 1 Chr 3:10 has *ʾāsāʾ* (Asa, the Judahite king). The Byzantine majority text + KJV harmonize to 'Asa'. The critical-text *Asaph* is widely-treated as either (a) a Matthean error / variant-source-list (Metzger 1994); (b) a deliberate-typological allusion to the psalmist (Davies-Allison ICC 1.176). The WoH-Translation preserves the critical-text *Asaph*.

paragraphs.text: Ἀσὰφ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσαφάτ, Ἰωσαφὰτ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωράμ, Ἰωρὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ὀζίαν,
paragraphs.translit: Asaph de egennēsen ton Iōsaphat, Iōsaphat de egennēsen ton Iōram, Iōram de egennēsen ton Ozian,

i18n.en: and Asaph begot Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat begot Joram, and Joram begot Uzziah,

paragraphs.text: Ὀζίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωαθάμ, Ἰωαθὰμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀχάζ, Ἀχὰζ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἑζεκίαν,
paragraphs.translit: Ozias de egennēsen ton Iōatham, Iōatham de egennēsen ton Achaz, Achaz de egennēsen ton Hezekian,

i18n.en: and Uzziah begot Jotham, and Jotham begot Ahaz, and Ahaz begot Hezekiah,

paragraphs.text: Ἑζεκίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Μανασσῆ, Μανασσῆς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀμώς, Ἀμὼς δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσίαν,
paragraphs.translit: Hezekias de egennēsen ton Manassē, Manassēs de egennēsen ton Amōs, Amōs de egennēsen ton Iōsian,

i18n.en: and Hezekiah begot Manasseh, and Manasseh begot Amos, and Amos begot Josiah,

notes.official: **Textual variant — parallel to v.7.** Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + critical text read *Amos* (the prophet's name); the Hebrew Bible 2 Kgs 21:18 has *ʾāmôn* (Amon, the Judahite king). The Byzantine majority + KJV harmonize. Either a variant-source-list / Matthean error or a deliberate-typological allusion to the prophet. Metzger 1994; Davies-Allison ICC 1.177-178.

paragraphs.text: Ἰωσίας δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰεχονίαν καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος.
paragraphs.translit: Iōsias de egennēsen ton Iechonian kai tous adelphous autou epi tēs metoikesias Babylōnos.

i18n.en: and Josiah begot Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the deportation to Babylon.

paragraphs.text: Μετὰ δὲ τὴν μετοικεσίαν Βαβυλῶνος Ἰεχονίας ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαλαθιήλ, Σαλαθιὴλ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ζοροβαβέλ,
paragraphs.translit: Meta de tēn metoikesian Babylōnos Iechonias egennēsen ton Salathiēl, Salathiēl de egennēsen ton Zorobabel,

i18n.en: And after the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah begot Salathiel, and Salathiel begot Zerubbabel,

paragraphs.text: Ζοροβαβὲλ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀβιούδ, Ἀβιοὺδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλιακίμ, Ἐλιακὶμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀζώρ,
paragraphs.translit: Zorobabel de egennēsen ton Abioud, Abioud de egennēsen ton Eliakim, Eliakim de egennēsen ton Azōr,

i18n.en: and Zerubbabel begot Abiud, and Abiud begot Eliakim, and Eliakim begot Azor,

paragraphs.text: Ἀζὼρ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Σαδώκ, Σαδὼκ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἀχίμ, Ἀχὶμ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλιούδ,
paragraphs.translit: Azōr de egennēsen ton Sadōk, Sadōk de egennēsen ton Achim, Achim de egennēsen ton Elioud,

i18n.en: and Azor begot Zadok, and Zadok begot Achim, and Achim begot Eliud,

paragraphs.text: Ἐλιοὺδ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἐλεάζαρ, Ἐλεάζαρ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ματθάν, Ματθὰν δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰακώβ,
paragraphs.translit: Elioud de egennēsen ton Eleazar, Eleazar de egennēsen ton Matthan, Matthan de egennēsen ton Iakōb,

i18n.en: and Eliud begot Eleazar, and Eleazar begot Matthan, and Matthan begot Jacob,

paragraphs.text: Ἰακὼβ δὲ ἐγέννησεν τὸν Ἰωσὴφ τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας, ἐξ ἧς ἐγεννήθη Ἰησοῦς ὁ λεγόμενος χριστός.
paragraphs.translit: Iakōb de egennēsen ton Iōsēph ton andra Marias, ex hēs egennēthē Iēsous ho legomenos christos.

i18n.en: and Jacob begot Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

notes.official: *ex hēs egennēthē* — the genealogical break: feminine relative *hēs* 'of whom' (referring to Mary, not Joseph) and the passive *egennēthē* 'was born' both signal the virgin-conception. The Matthean grammar breaks the otherwise-active masculine-begetting pattern of the genealogy. A small group of witnesses (Sinaitic Syriac, some Old Latin) reads 'Joseph begot Jesus' — generally rejected as harmonizing-adoptionist. Davies-Allison ICC 1.183-184; Brown 1993 138-139.

paragraphs.text: Πᾶσαι οὖν αἱ γενεαὶ ἀπὸ Ἀβραὰμ ἕως Δαυὶδ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ ἀπὸ Δαυὶδ ἕως τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες, καὶ ἀπὸ τῆς μετοικεσίας Βαβυλῶνος ἕως τοῦ χριστοῦ γενεαὶ δεκατέσσαρες.
paragraphs.translit: Pasai oun hai geneai apo Abraam heōs Dauid geneai dekatessares, kai apo Dauid heōs tēs metoikesias Babylōnos geneai dekatessares, kai apo tēs metoikesias Babylōnos heōs tou christou geneai dekatessares.

i18n.en: So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations, and from David to the deportation to Babylon fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ fourteen generations.

notes.official: **Schematic 14×3 generation-pattern.** 14 = 2×7 (sevenfold-completion doubled); 14 also equals the gematria of DWD = דוד (D=4 + W=6 + D=4 = 14), David's name. The strict arithmetic counts 14+14+13 names (third section missing one), so the schema is interpretive-intent over strict-arithmetic. The triple-fourteen structures the Davidic-line and positions the Messiah at the 3×14 = 42 = 6×7 climax of the typological-schema. Davies-Allison ICC 1.161-165; Brown 1993 74-84.

paragraphs.text: Τοῦ δὲ Ἰησοῦ χριστοῦ ἡ γένεσις οὕτως ἦν. μνηστευθείσης τῆς μητρὸς αὐτοῦ Μαρίας τῷ Ἰωσήφ, πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν αὐτοὺς εὑρέθη ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου.
paragraphs.translit: Tou de Iēsou christou hē genesis houtōs ēn. mnēsteutheisēs tēs mētros autou Marias tō Iōsēph, prin ē synelthein autous heurethē en gastri echousa ek pneumatos hagiou.

i18n.en: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was in this way. When his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together she was found to be with child of the Holy Spirit.

notes.official: *ek pneumatos hagiou* — 'of [a] holy spirit' (anarthrous). The Greek lacks the definite article, which in 1st-c. usage does NOT yet carry the fully-developed Trinitarian Holy-Spirit-as-third-person sense (a 4th-c. theological development). Brown 1993 124-125 cautions against retrojecting Nicene Trinitarian theology onto the 1st-c. anarthrous phrase. Davies-Allison ICC 1.200-203 treat the conception-narrative against the OT divine-conception background (Gen 18 Sarah; 1 Sam 1 Hannah — but the Matthean *ek pneumatos hagiou* has no direct Hebrew Bible parallel for human-virginal-conception). The lens-risk site is preserved without surface-pre-resolution.

paragraphs.text: Ἰωσὴφ δὲ ὁ ἀνὴρ αὐτῆς, δίκαιος ὢν καὶ μὴ θέλων αὐτὴν δειγματίσαι, ἐβουλήθη λάθρᾳ ἀπολῦσαι αὐτήν.
paragraphs.translit: Iōsēph de ho anēr autēs, dikaios ōn kai mē thelōn autēn deigmatisai, eboulēthē lathra apolysai autēn.

i18n.en: And Joseph her husband, being a righteous man and not wishing to expose her to disgrace, resolved to divorce her quietly.

notes.official: *dikaios ōn* — the Matthean characterization of Joseph as 'righteous'. Two interpretive readings: (a) Joseph is law-observant (Deut 22:23-24 prescribes the death-penalty for adultery), and so obliged-to-divorce, but compassionately; (b) Joseph is righteous-as-merciful and refuses to expose Mary publicly. Both readings have ancient and modern defenders. Davies-Allison ICC 1.202-204; Brown 1993 125-128. The translation preserves the ambiguity.

paragraphs.text: ταῦτα δὲ αὐτοῦ ἐνθυμηθέντος ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου κατ' ὄναρ ἐφάνη αὐτῷ λέγων· Ἰωσὴφ υἱὸς Δαυίδ, μὴ φοβηθῇς παραλαβεῖν Μαρίαν τὴν γυναῖκά σου, τὸ γὰρ ἐν αὐτῇ γεννηθὲν ἐκ πνεύματός ἐστιν ἁγίου·
paragraphs.translit: tauta de autou enthymēthentos idou angelos kyriou kat' onar ephanē autō legōn· Iōsēph huios Dauid, mē phobēthēs paralabein Marian tēn gynaika sou, to gar en autē gennēthen ek pneumatos estin hagiou·

i18n.en: But while he was considering these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying: "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for that which has been conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.

notes.official: *angelos kyriou kat' onar* — the dream-vision angelophany. The phrase *angelos kyriou* directly calques the LXX rendering of *malʾakh YHWH* (the messenger-of-YHWH), the recurring Hebrew Bible theophanic-figure (Gen 16:7; Ex 3:2; Judg 13). The first of Joseph's four dream-revelations in Matthew (1:20; 2:13; 2:19; 2:22) — a Matthean Joseph-typological pattern echoing the Genesis Joseph (Gen 37 + 40-41) who likewise receives revelation through dreams. Davies-Allison ICC 1.204-207.

paragraphs.text: τέξεται δὲ υἱὸν καὶ καλέσεις τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν, αὐτὸς γὰρ σώσει τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: texetai de huion kai kaleseis to onoma autou Iēsoun, autos gar sōsei ton laon autou apo tōn hamartiōn autōn.

i18n.en: She will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins."

notes.official: **In-verse folk-etymology.** *Iēsoun ... sōsei* — the Greek wordplay implicit (both -s-words); the Hebrew wordplay direct: *Yēšûaʿ* (Jesus) from root *yšʿ* 'to save' + the Yāh-theophoric → 'YHWH saves'. The angel-of-the-Lord explicitly invokes the *yšʿ*-element of the name as rationale for the naming. The closest typological-pattern is Sir 46:1 (the post-exilic Hebrew Sirach on Joshua-son-of-Nun: *gibbôr ba-milḥāmâ ... le-hôšîaʿ ʾet bĕḥîrāyw* 'a warrior in battle ... to save his chosen'). Davies-Allison ICC 1.209; Brown 1993 130-131.

paragraphs.text: τοῦτο δὲ ὅλον γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν ὑπὸ κυρίου διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
paragraphs.translit: touto de holon gegonen hina plērōthē to rhēthen hypo kyriou dia tou prophētou legontos·

i18n.en: Now all this took place so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:

notes.official: *hina plērōthē* — the first of Matthew's signature fulfillment-formulae (occurring 12x: Mt 1:22; 2:15; 2:17-18; 2:23; 4:14-16; 8:17; 12:17-21; 13:14-15; 13:35; 21:4-5; 27:9-10). The formula explicitly frames the Gospel as eschatological-fulfillment of Israel's scriptures. The semantic breadth of *plēroō* (cf. central entry `abolish-or-fulfill-mt-5-17-katalysai-vs-plērōsai-christian-supersessionism-disavowal-cross-corpus`) supports both 'fulfill prophecy' and 'bring to true-meaning fullness'. Davies-Allison ICC 1.209-213.

paragraphs.text: Ἰδοὺ ἡ παρθένος ἐν γαστρὶ ἕξει καὶ τέξεται υἱόν, καὶ καλέσουσιν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἐμμανουήλ· ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Μεθ' ἡμῶν ὁ θεός.
paragraphs.translit: Idou hē parthenos en gastri hexei kai texetai huion, kai kalesousin to onoma autou Emmanouēl· ho estin methermēneuomenon Meth' hēmōn ho theos.

i18n.en: "Behold, the virgin shall be with child and shall bear a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel" — which is translated, "God with us."

notes.official:
**Major philological crux: Isa 7:14 LXX parthenos vs Hebrew ʿalmâ.** Matthew cites the LXX *parthenos* 'virgin'; the Hebrew MT reads *ʿalmâ* 'young woman of marriageable age' (technical Hebrew virgin = *bĕtûlâ*). The Isa 7:14 oracle in its 8th-c. BCE setting addresses King Ahaz during the Syro-Ephraimite crisis; the immediate-historical referent (wife of Ahaz / Isaiah / Davidic-house figure) is debated. The Jewish-Christian philological dispute dates to Justin Martyr's *Dialogue with Trypho* 71-77 (c. 155-160 CE). The WoH-Translation preserves the LXX-text Matthew cites without adjudicating the underlying Hebrew dispute — see `isa-7-14-virgin-birth-mt-1-22-23-parthenos-vs-almah-philological-dispute-cross-corpus`.

*Emmanouēl ... Meth' hēmōn ho theos* — the Matthean calque of Hebrew *ʿimmānû-ʾēl* 'with-us is El'. The Emmanuel-naming opens the Matthean structural-inclusio that closes at Mt 28:20 *meth' hymōn eimi* 'I am with you' — D. D. Kupp, *Matthew's Emmanuel* (SNTSMS 90, Cambridge 1996), the comprehensive monograph. See `emmanuel-frame-inclusio-mt-1-23-mt-28-20-divine-presence-cross-corpus-kupp`.

paragraphs.text: ἐγερθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰωσὴφ ἀπὸ τοῦ ὕπνου ἐποίησεν ὡς προσέταξεν αὐτῷ ὁ ἄγγελος κυρίου καὶ παρέλαβεν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: egertheis de ho Iōsēph apo tou hypnou epoiēsen hōs prosetaxen autō ho angelos kyriou kai parelaben tēn gynaika autou·

i18n.en: And Joseph, rising from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him, and took his wife,

paragraphs.text: καὶ οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν αὐτὴν ἕως οὗ ἔτεκεν υἱόν· καὶ ἐκάλεσεν τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ Ἰησοῦν.
paragraphs.translit: kai ouk eginōsken autēn heōs hou eteken huion· kai ekalesen to onoma autou Iēsoun.

i18n.en: and did not know her until she had borne a son; and he called his name Jesus.

notes.official: *ouk eginōsken autēn heōs hou eteken huion* — the imperfect *eginōsken* + *heōs* 'until' construction. The Catholic-Orthodox perpetual-virginity tradition reads *heōs* as terminating-no-implication (i.e., the relationship-status before-the-birth is asserted; what happens after is not implied); the Protestant tradition reads *heōs* as terminating-with-implication (i.e., the relationship-status changes after the birth). The Greek admits both readings; cf. Mt 28:20 *meth' hymōn eimi pasas tas hēmeras heōs tēs synteleias tou aiōnos* where *heōs* clearly does NOT imply termination. Textual variant: some Byzantine MSS add *ton prōtotokon* 'the firstborn' (KJV); absent in B + א + critical text. Davies-Allison ICC 1.218-219; Brown 1993 132-134.
